model_annotation: This line plot illustrates the coverage performance of four different Llama model variants—Llama-3B, Llama-3B + FT, Llama-1B, and Llama-1B + FT—as a function of the number of completions (k), which ranges from 2⁰ to 2⁸ on a logarithmic x-axis. The y-axis, labeled “Coverage,” spans from 0.2 to 1.0 in linear scale, with major tick marks at intervals of 0.2. The Llama-3B model (solid blue line with circle markers) starts at approximately 0.43 coverage at k=1 and steadily increases to about 0.90 at k=256. The Llama-3B + FT variant (dashed green line with triangle markers) begins slightly higher at ~0.45 and rises to ~0.92 at k=256, consistently outperforming the base Llama-3B. The Llama-1B model (solid light blue line with square markers) starts at ~0.28 and climbs to ~0.85, while the Llama-1B + FT variant (dashed light green line with diamond markers) begins at ~0.30 and reaches ~0.87, also showing a consistent improvement over its base counterpart. All lines exhibit a monotonically increasing trend, with steeper gains at lower k values and diminishing returns as k increases.
